b.sound: People liked that he wrote in Scots and represented Scotland.
People liked that he wrote in French and represented France.

atoms.b: In 1707, Scotland and England had united to become ((++Great_Britain London)). This meant that Scotland was less independent and fewer people spoke Scots.
Burns’ poetry became very popular because he wrote in ((++Scots French)) when not many others did, and he was very proud to be Scottish.
atoms.sound: Burns’s poetry became very popular because he wrote in Scots when not many others did, and he was very proud to be Scottish.

feedback.end: Lots of Scottish people felt very connected to Robert Burns. They affectionately called him Rabbie, the Scottish nickname for Robert.

instruction.text: In 1787, Burns decided to travel throughout Scotland to learn even more about his country. Find the cities in Scotland that he travelled to.

feedback.finish: While he was on this trip, Burns learnt about Scottish history and old Scottish songs that he could use for his poetry.
